analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 23rd November
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 3.7% and Nasdaq-100 fell 5.6% last week, the worst week since Mar-20, led by a fragile AI/Capex narrative. Cross-asset action signalled a broader growth slowdown.
NVDA fell 14% to an 18-month low on a report of an SEC accounting probe and dragged SOXX down 10%. AAPL (+0.5%) and GOOGL (+0.4%) were rare bright spots and Staples was the only sector in the green.
US futures are bouncing this morning (Nasdaq +3%, S&P +2%) after Bessent warned the Fed risks overtightening. EStoxx is up 50bps.
Asia is stabilising as authorities step in. Taiex is up 2% and Kospi is down 3%, better than signalled after Seoul said it stands ready to deploy stabilisation funds immediately.
SK Hynix is in focus on reports that SoftBank's Son weighed a $1tr bid before shelving the idea.
The desk draws parallels with Q4 2018: sharp rotation then a correction into a hawkish December Fed. This time the AI fear is new.
Thanksgiving week is seasonally supportive (S&P +71bps average over 30 years, 63% hit rate). In 2018 the S&P fell 3.8% that week before rallying 28.8% in 2019.
The desk calls for a low participation and volume recovery this week. The AI Capex story lacks a definitive short-term catalyst.
The Dec Fed meeting is rising in importance, with 93% priced for a 25bp hike. Waller is the dissenter and the Fed blackout runs 28 Nov to 10 Dec.

Week ahead macro risk is concentrated on Wednesday with October PCE, GDP, personal income, durable goods, new home sales, claims and the Beige Book. It is the last major inflation read before the December Fed.

Other week-ahead events: Monday flash PMIs, Tuesday German IFO and US consumer confidence, Thursday US holiday and European Council on Ukraine financing and the next ECB president, Friday France sovereign rating review.
Earnings this week are led by Dell, HP, HPE, Analog Devices, Autodesk, Workday, Deere and Medtronic, plus Xiaomi, Meituan, Li Auto, Compass and Prosus.
Friday flows were marginally better for sale (54/46). Healthcare was busiest (20% of turnover) and better to buy, while Technology (11%) saw supply in semis and software.

tension_points.bull_case: Thanksgiving week is seasonally positive (S&P +71bps average, 63% hit rate) and futures are bouncing on Bessent's overtightening warning.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI Capex story lacks a definitive short-term catalyst, and in 2018 the S&P fell 3.8% in the same week before the December Fed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A firm FOMC stance into the Dec meeting with 93% priced for a hike, with Waller as the lone dissenter, would undermine the rally.
